source.citation: Grunewald et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2022, DOI: 10.1021/acs.jctc.2c00757, Table S2 (Experimental partitioning coefficients)
source.note: Glucose and Trehalose carry the values the cited table reports, with the table's own standard deviations over n = 3. Sucrose and Maltose appear nowhere in that table, so their datasets stay metadata-only: they need an experimental water-octanol partitioning source of their own, and no uncertainty has been invented for them. Table S2's Exp column is a partition free energy in kJ/mol and equals 5.708 x logP for every row in it (checked against all eleven), so the unit and the convention are the table's rather than an interpretation of ours.

targets.name: D-glucose, water-octanol partition free energy
targets.conditions: 25 C, water-octanol; Table S2's Exp column, which equals 5.708 x logP with logP = -3.12; uncertainty is the table's SD over n = 3

datasets.missing: Sucrose is not a row in the cited table; a water-octanol partitioning measurement with a stated uncertainty is needed, as Trehalose's row has (it cites 10.1016/j.carres.2004.12.038 for its logP).

targets.name: Trehalose, water-octanol partition free energy
targets.conditions: 25 C, water-octanol; Table S2's Exp column, which equals 5.708 x logP with logP = -3.77 (that logP is taken from 10.1016/j.carres.2004.12.038); uncertainty is the table's SD over n = 3

datasets.missing: Maltose appears nowhere in the cited table (nor in its supporting information), so it needs its own experimental source, matched to the same quantity and temperature.
